newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken says to take part in structural changes.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken says to take part in structural changes.

text.p: Swedish banking group S-E-Banken said on Thursday it expected restructuring of the banking sector to continue and that it would take part in these changes if they benefited its priority markets.

"S-E-Banken already has today a strong position among large and mid-sized companies as well as among private customers with money to invest," said chairman Karl-Erik Sahlberg and chief executive Bjorn Svedberg in the bank's 1996 annual report.
"We will guard and strengthen that position. We will keep following developments and take an active part in structural changes when they benefit the markets we see as a long-term priority."
S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken were in merger talks earlier this year but negotiations collapsed in February.

Market players have speculated that merger talks between the two banks could resume later this year after a change of guard at S-E-Banken with Jacob Wallenberg taking over from Svedberg as chief executive.
